Chapter 9 • Newton-Cartan Theory

9.5 Gravity in the Connection

  • With gravity, the observation changes. In a stratified chart \((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\) with Cartesian spatial coordinates, non-rotating axes and origin at rest w.r.t. the sources, every freely falling body obeys \(\ddot{\gamma}^\alpha_\mathcal{U} = - \partial x_\alpha\left\lfloor \phi \right\rceil\), independently of its velocity and mass, where \(\phi \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})\) satisfies \(\Delta \phi \coloneqq \sum_{\alpha} \partial x_\alpha\left\lfloor \partial x_\alpha\left\lfloor \phi \right\rceil \right\rceil = 4 \pi G_N \rho\). Matching coefficients gives \begin{align*} \Gamma^\alpha_{00} = \partial x_\alpha\left\lfloor \phi \right\rceil, \qquad \text{all other } \Gamma^i_{jk} = 0 \longrightarrow m \, \ddot{\gamma}^\alpha_\mathcal{U}(t) = - m \, \partial_\alpha \left[ \phi \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right] \big( \mathscr{X}(\gamma(t)) \big), \end{align*} where no further forces act, \(f^\alpha_\gamma = 0\). For a point mass \(M\) at the spatial origin, \(\left( \phi \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \right)(t, \xi) = - G_N M / |\xi|\), with \(|\xi| \coloneqq \sqrt{\textstyle\sum_\beta (\xi^\beta)^2}\), and this reduces to Newton’s law of universal gravitation, \begin{align*} m \, \ddot{\gamma}^\alpha_\mathcal{U}(t) = - \frac{G M m}{|\gamma_\mathcal{U}(t)|^3} \, \gamma^\alpha_\mathcal{U}(t), \qquad |\gamma_\mathcal{U}| \coloneqq \sqrt{\textstyle\sum_\beta \big( \gamma^\beta_\mathcal{U} \big)^2}. \end{align*} Gravity thus moves from the forces into the connection. Note that, in other stratified charts, \(\Gamma^\alpha_{00}\) mixes gravity with pseudo-forces, which only the curvature separates.

  • Gravity occupies the same slot, \(\Gamma^\alpha_{00}\), as the translational pseudo-force, which raises the question whether it is a pseudo-force too. The answer depends on whether the gravitational field is uniform.

    1. Uniform gravity is a pseudo-force. If \(\partial x_\alpha\left\lfloor \phi \right\rceil\) is the same at every point, the chart \((\mathcal{V}, \mathscr{Y})\) with \(\xi^\alpha = \eta^\alpha + b^\alpha(t)\) and \(\ddot{b}^\alpha = - \partial x_\alpha\left\lfloor \phi \right\rceil\), whose origin falls freely, has \(\Gamma^\alpha_{00} = \partial x_\alpha\left\lfloor \phi \right\rceil + \ddot{b}^\alpha = 0\): in a freely falling elevator, uniform gravity disappears completely.

    2. Non-uniform gravity is not. The quadratic terms of the Riemann curvature vanish, since \(\Gamma^r_{jm} \neq 0\) requires \(r\) spatial and then \(\Gamma^i_{rk} = 0\), and its only non-vanishing component functions are \begin{align*} \mathrm{Riem}^\alpha_{0\beta0} = - \mathrm{Riem}^\alpha_{00\beta} = \partial x_\beta\left\lfloor \partial x_\alpha\left\lfloor \phi \right\rceil \right\rceil. \end{align*} Wherever the gravitational field varies from point to point, \(\mathrm{Riem} \neq 0\) in this chart, hence in every chart, and no choice of chart removes it.

  • Spacetime, not space, is curved: \(\mathrm{Riem}^\alpha_{\beta\delta\kappa} = 0\), while every non-vanishing component carries the time index twice.

9.5.1 Field Equation

  • Poisson’s equation, which determines \(\phi\) from \(\rho\), can be written in terms of the connection. The only non-vanishing component function of the Ricci curvature is \(\mathrm{Ric}_{00} = \mathrm{Riem}^\alpha_{0\alpha0} = \Delta \phi = 4 \pi G_N \rho\), and in a stratified chart \(dt\left\lceil \partial x_i \right\rfloor = \delta^0_i\). Both facts combine into the chart-independent statement \begin{align*} \mathrm{Ric}(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}) = 4 \pi G_N \rho \; dt\left\lceil \mathcal{X} \right\rfloor \, dt\left\lceil \mathcal{Y} \right\rfloor, \qquad \forall \, \mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y} \in \Gamma T\mathcal{M}, \end{align*} which, both sides being \(C^\infty(\mathcal{M})\)-bilinear, holds in every chart once verified in one.

  • Matter determines the Ricci curvature, and the curvature determines free fall: this is the time-time component of the Einstein equations.

9.5.2 Tidal Acceleration

  • Although non-uniform gravity cannot be removed globally, it can be removed along a single worldline, which is the content of the equivalence principle. Let \(\Phi \coloneqq \phi \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}\), a function of \(\xi\), and consider again the chart \(\xi^\alpha = \eta^\alpha + b^\alpha(t)\), now with an origin falling freely in the non-uniform field, \(\ddot{b}^\alpha(t) = - \partial_\alpha \Phi\big( t, b(t) \big)\). Expanding around the origin, \begin{align*} \left( \Gamma_\mathscr{Y} \right)^\alpha_{00}(t, \eta) = \partial_\alpha \Phi\big( t, \eta + b(t) \big) + \ddot{b}^\alpha(t) = \partial_\beta \partial_\alpha \Phi\big( t, b(t) \big) \, \eta^\beta + \mathcal{O}\big( |\eta|^2 \big), \end{align*} which vanishes at the origin, \(\eta = 0\): an observer falling with it feels no gravity.

  • For a second freely falling particle, with spatial coordinates \(\gamma^\alpha_\mathcal{V}\), Newton I gives \begin{align*} \ddot{\gamma}^\alpha_\mathcal{V} = - \mathrm{Riem}^\alpha_{0\beta0} \, \gamma^\beta_\mathcal{V} + \mathcal{O}\big( |\gamma_\mathcal{V}|^2 \big), \end{align*} with \(\mathrm{Riem}^\alpha_{0\beta0} = \partial_\beta \partial_\alpha \Phi\big( t, b(t) \big)\) evaluated at the origin. What survives in the falling chart is the relative acceleration of neighbouring free particles, the tidal acceleration, determined by the Riemann curvature: the part of gravity that cannot be transformed away.
